carousel.short: The better apartment on the table.
carousel.long: The better apartment on the table. After the plot lost part of its buildable area, our architect proposed merging a small studio and a one-bedroom at the rear into one generous T2 with its own patio. As architecture, it was the right call.

carousel.short: Two easy sales, or one hard one.
carousel.long: Two easy sales, or one hard one. As a product, the merge turned two easy sales into one hard one. So we kept two registered units: one buyer can use them as one home, or as two.

carousel.short: Diagram: Two easy sales, not one hard one.
carousel.long: Diagram: Two easy sales, not one hard one. One buyer, two units: live as one, or rent as two.

Balconies go before the interior. When a site loses area, give up the balconies first. Smaller units keep the price range adjustable, even at a higher price per metre, and a cramped one may need height, not width. And the rear stair? We're making it a feature.

carousel.short: The better apartment is one conversation, what the market can buy is the other, and a project…
carousel.long: The better apartment is one conversation, what the market can buy is the other, and a project needs both. Working through a unit mix right now? I'm happy to compare notes.
